claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace defeats the arrival limb. All 34 driver fixes in EV-GPS-09105 sit 219.77 m from the pickup pin (min, mean and max distance are identical, and trace_distance_km is 0.0), and the derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count of 0 — not one fix falls inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, and under POL-NS-02 that failure entitles the rider to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The in-geofence dwell is zero, so the waiting-period condition fails independently of the arrival limb. The driver's trace runs from 13:05:00 to cancellation at 13:10:30 with every fix at 0.0 km/h and zero distance travelled, but at 219.77 m from the pin, so the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup — a 300 second shortfall. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive: all four limbs must hold and any single failure makes the fee unchargeable. I accept that limb (a) is met (trip_record arrived_at 13:05:20) and that limb (d) is met (terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW), but limbs (b) and (c) both fail on the trace — no qualifying in-radius fix and no qualifying dwell. Two broken limbs, not one, defeat the charge.

This is the wrong-entrance case that POL-NS-03 governs. The driver was stationary — all fixes 0.0 km/h and trace_distance_km 0.0 — for 330 seconds, from 13:05:00 to the 13:10:30 cancellation, which is longer than the required 300 second dwell, at a point 219.77 m from the pickup pin: outside the 120 m POL-NS-02 arrival radius but comfortably inside the 400 m ceiling that is the whole test. On those numbers the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. POL-NS-05 is not engaged on these numbers (219.77 m is short of 300 m and the driver was not moving), and POL-NS-05 itself directs a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03.

Fault sits with the driver, so no compensation is payable to him. The chat log shows the rider naming the correct sub-location twice — 'I am at Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign' at 13:05:05 and 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' at 13:06:35 — while the driver had posted at 13:06:00 that he was at the mall taxi stand and never moved before cancelling at 13:10:30. That is the driver's own account on file: he waited at a mall entrance for the timer and did not move to Tower B. Under POL-NS-03(i), where the rider stated the correct entrance, block or tower in the chat log and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. The pin-ambiguity goodwill in limb (ii) is unavailable because it requires that neither party specified a sub-location, and the rider plainly did.

The driver cannot rebuild a dwell under POL-NS-06(i). The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09105-01, is MISSING — status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, weight_multiplier 0.0, payload null — so no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT advisory covers this pickup road and waiting window, and limb (i) is unavailable on its own terms. I rely on that artifact for its absence, which is itself citable. In any event there is nothing to accumulate: the trace records run_count 0 and accumulated dwell 0.0 seconds, i.e. no in-geofence interval existed at all.

The rider was at the pin rather than absent, which answers the driver's account that he was left waiting for a rider who never came. The rider track in EV-GPS-09105 carries 16 fixes, every one of them 25.0 m from the pickup pin (min and mean identical) and therefore inside the 150 m rider-presence measure that POL-NS-04 limb (c) sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 16 of 16. I put this forward as the presence test POL-NS-04 limb (c) defines rather than as a full limb (a)-to-(c) case, since the driver did reply at 13:06:00 within 120 seconds of the rider's first message; the rider's position also disposes of any suggestion that the rider's own absence explains the failed pickup.

The driver's compensation route is closed on this record. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here POL-NS-01 fails at limbs (b) and (c), and both POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 displace it. No compensation is payable to the driver, and the rider should not be charged over so that any payout can be funded.

The rider presently carries the disputed charge and needs the cancellation-fee line refunded. EV-FARE-09105 records cancellation_fee 4.00 SGD, total_charged 4.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, against a LARGE_VENUE pickup in an RYDE_X vehicle — the 4.00 SGD figure the fee schedule prescribes for both those dimensions, so no amount is in issue, only whether it may be kept. Because this dispute is filed by the rider, a NO_ACTION outcome would leave that 4.00 SGD charge standing under POL-GEN-03; the rider needs the cancellation-fee line refunded and nothing else on the fare is in dispute.

claims.text: The trip_record 'arrived' marker is not a false arrival under POL-NS-05. At the 13:05:20 event the GPS trace places the driver stationary — 0.0 kph across all 34 fixes — at a mean 219.77 m from the pickup pin, which is inside POL-NS-05's 300 m ceiling and nothing like its 15 km/h motion trigger. POL-NS-05 therefore catches nothing: the driver is not to be written up as a false-arrival offender, the waiting period is not voided on that ground, and the case is decided under POL-NS-03.

The driver was at the venue and held his ground for the whole waiting window: 34 fixes at 0.0 kph, continuous from 13:05:00 to 13:10:30 — 330 seconds, more than the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum — all at 219.77 m from the pin. That is outside the 120 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for LARGE_VENUE but comfortably inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, which is precisely the wrong-entrance situation POL-NS-03 was written for. The fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 limb (b), and POL-NS-03 governs.

Both parties were on the same mall site, at different faces of it, and that is established from party statements in the chat log, not from geography: the driver posted at 13:06:00 'I am waiting at the mall taxi stand' and the rider answered at 13:06:35 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' This is the ordinary Singapore wrong-entrance case inside one LARGE_VENUE site carrying 3 registered pickup points, and the mislocation is between two signed points of that single venue.

On POL-NS-03(ii) the driver is owed the platform-funded pin-ambiguity goodwill of 50 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 2.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. The limb's second condition is satisfied outright: trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 3, above the threshold of 2. The first condition is satisfied as well, because neither party specified a sub-location: the rider's 13:05:05 message repeats the pickup pin's own label word for word ('Tower B ride-hail pickup'), and the driver's 13:06:00 message names only the mall taxi stand — neither party identified which of the three registered pickup points was to be used. The mislocation is therefore attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party.

POL-NS-04 does not apply and cannot strip the driver of compensation. The clause is conjunctive and limb (b) is not met: the rider's locating message at 13:05:05 drew the driver's reply at 13:06:00, 55 seconds later and well inside the 120 second window, and the exchange continued on both sides through the waiting window. The clause's target is an unanswered rider; that is not this trip, so the dispute stays under POL-NS-03 where the driver's goodwill payment is assessed.

Nothing in the bundle is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08, so the facts that decide this case carry full weight and none of the POL-NS-09 escalation triggers fires. The 13:05:20 'arrived' event sits within one 10 second sampling interval of the nearest fix (no clock skew, no gap, 34 fixes across the window); the chat log holds all 4 messages that trip_record.chat_message_count records, with no break in its msg_id sequence; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee exactly equals fee_schedule.resolution_rule for LARGE_VENUE (SGD 4.00) against RYDE_X (SGD 4.00). The driver's entitlement can be ruled on at full confidence.

The driver's pin-ambiguity goodwill is an independent payment under POL-GEN-03 and is not netted against anything else in the case: the SGD 2.00 is platform-funded and payable to the driver for the mislocation, and it stands on its own rather than being offset against the rider's side of the ledger.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full. The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-09105) puts every one of his 34 fixes 219.77 m from the Tower B pickup pin, stationary at 0.0 kph for the whole window — so no fix ever falls inside the 120 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for this LARGE_VENUE pickup (qualifying_fix_count = 0), and there is likewise no qualifying in-geofence dwell (0.0 s against the 300 s minimum). POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) both fail, and the fee is not chargeable. POL-NS-03 then governs, because the driver was stationary for the full waiting period within its 400 m ceiling: this is a wrong-entrance case. On fault, POL-NS-03(i) applies — you named the correct tower in the chat log at 13:05:05 ('Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign') and again at 13:06:35 ('That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.'), and the driver did not move to it before cancelling at 13:10:30 — so the driver bears the loss and receives nothing.

To the driver: I accept your account that you waited at a mall entrance for the full timer and did not move to Tower B, and the trace confirms you held position throughout. But that position was 219.77 m from the pin, outside the 120 m arrival radius for a large-venue pickup, so under POL-NS-01(b) you did not arrive at the pickup point and the fee cannot stand; POL-NS-02 is 'subject to POL-NS-03', and POL-NS-03 refunds the rider in full on these facts. You are not caught by POL-NS-05: you were stationary, trace_distance_km 0.0, and well inside its 300 m ceiling, so no false-arrival finding is recorded against you in the referrals. Your claim to the SGD 2.00 pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03(ii) does not succeed: that limb requires that neither party specified a sub-location, and the rider did specify Tower B, twice, while you remained at the mall taxi stand. Limb (i) therefore applies and the residual 20 percent/50 percent reasoning is not reached. Independently, POL-NS-04 does not apply (you replied within 120 seconds) but that is not what decides your compensation, and POL-NS-07 pays nothing because POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-03 displaces it.

On the evidence: nothing is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08. The 13:05:20 'arrived' event sits within one 10 s sampling interval of the nearest fix (no clock skew), the trace has no gaps and 34 fixes across the window, the chat log holds all 4 messages trip_record.chat_message_count records with no break in its msg_id sequence, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee reconciles with the fee schedule (greater of LARGE_VENUE SGD 4.00 and RYDE_X SGD 4.00). The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09105-01, weight 0.0) is relied on only for its absence, which is citable, and no clause needs it to be present. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at full weight 1.0, so no POL-NS-09 trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifacts contradict each other, the counterparty-dispute counts are 0, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, not 4 or more). The charge stands unpaid-of nothing further: SGD 4.00 is returned to you, the rider.

To both parties. The pickup was at NEX Serangoon, a LARGE_VENUE site (arrival radius 120 m, minimum dwell 300 seconds). The driver's own GPS trace places all 34 fixes, from 13:05:00 to the 13:10:30 cancellation, at 219.77 m from the Tower B pickup pin, with the vehicle stationary throughout (0.0 km/h, 0.0 km travelled). The driver never entered the 120 m arrival geofence, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and limb (c) fails with it (in-geofence dwell 0 seconds against the 300-second minimum). POL-NS-02 yields to POL-NS-03, because the driver was stationary for the full required dwell within 400 m of the pin: that is the wrong-entrance situation POL-NS-03 governs, and the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full (SGD 4.00). POL-NS-06 supplies a second, independent ground for the same result - the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds, and the accumulation rule in its limb (i) is unavailable because the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09105-01, is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, weight 0.0, payload null), so there is nothing to sum. On each of these tests the result has run and the refund follows.

On driver compensation: the chat log shows the rider twice stating the correct sub-location - 'Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign' at 13:05:05 and 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' at 13:06:35 - while the driver posted at 13:06:00 that he was at the mall taxi stand and, on his own statement, 'did not move to Tower B' before cancelling. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. The driver's argument for the platform-funded pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03(ii) is rejected: that limb applies only where NEITHER party specified a sub-location and there are 2 or more registered pickup points, and while the site does carry 3 points, the rider did specify the tower, so the first condition is not met. POL-NS-07 does not pay either, because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-03 displaces it. POL-NS-05 is not engaged - at the arrival marker the driver was stationary and within 300 m of the pin, well short of its 15 km/h trigger - so the arrival marker is not FALSE and no false-arrival referral is recorded. POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied within 120 seconds (55 seconds after the rider's first message), so its limb (b) fails.

Nothing in the bundle is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(a)-(d): the arrived event sits exactly on a 10-second GPS fix (no clock skew), the trace has no gap and 34 fixes across the waiting window, the chat log holds all 4 messages the trip record counts, and the SGD 4.00 fee reconciles with the fee schedule (LARGE_VENUE SGD 4.00 against RYDE_X SGD 4.00, the greater being SGD 4.00). No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 (GPS trace, trip record, chat log), so confidence is 0.90.

To both parties: the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is payable to the driver.

The facts are settled by the driver's own GPS trace. Across the entire waiting window (13:05:00 to the 13:10:30 cancellation, 34 fixes, every one at 0.0 km/h and zero distance travelled) the driver's position was a constant 219.77 m from the Tower B pickup pin. That is outside the 120 m arrival radius that applies to a LARGE_VENUE pickup, so not one fix qualifies as an in-geofence arrival (qualifying_fix_count 0). POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and limbs (b) and (c) both fail: the driver never entered the pickup geofence and the in-geofence dwell is zero against a 300 second minimum. The fee is therefore not chargeable, and the rider's claims on this point are accepted.

Because the driver did hold position for longer than the required 300 seconds (about 330 seconds) at a point within 400 m of the pin, this is the wrong-entrance situation POL-NS-03 was written for, and POL-NS-02 yields to it. The 400 m ceiling is met and the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. POL-NS-06 reaches the same full-refund result on the zero dwell, but POL-NS-03 governs the allocation of fault.

On the driver's claim for the 50 percent pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03(ii): it is refused. That limb applies only where neither party specified a sub-location. The rider named the tower in the chat at 13:05:05 ('I am at Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign') and again at 13:06:35 ('Please come to Tower B'), and the driver's own written account states he 'did not move to Tower B.' Limb (i) therefore applies — the rider stated the correct tower and the driver did not move to it before cancelling — so the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. The argument that the rider merely repeated the pin's own label does not change this: naming the correct tower is exactly what limb (i) requires, and limb (ii) is closed once a sub-location has been stated.

POL-NS-04 does not apply, as both sides accept, because the driver replied in chat within 120 seconds of the rider's first message; it neither helps nor harms the driver here. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the record agrees on the material facts, and they decide this case.

The pickup was NEX Serangoon, Tower B ride-hail pickup — a LARGE_VENUE zone, so a 120 m arrival radius and a 300-second minimum dwell (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01(c)). The driver's own trace, EV-GPS-09105, shows all 34 of his fixes at 219.77 m from the pickup pin, stationary at 0.0 km/h, from 13:05:00 through the 13:10:30 cancellation. He was never inside the 120 m arrival geofence: the trace's qualifying in-radius fix count is 0, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and with no in-geofence fix there is no qualifying dwell at all against the 300-second minimum, so limb (c) fails too. The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full. This is also the wrong-entrance situation POL-NS-03 was written for: stationary for 330 seconds (more than the required 300), outside the arrival radius but well inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, and the clause's own direction is a full refund. Both advocates' refund points (the rider's arrival and dwell claims, and the driver's POL-NS-03 characterisation) are accepted and lead to the same result.

POL-NS-05 catches nothing here: 219.77 m is short of its 300 m ceiling and the driver was not moving, so the arrival marker is not a false arrival, no false-arrival record is opened, and no referral issues.

Driver compensation: none is payable, and the driver's request for the SGD 2.00 pin-ambiguity goodwill is rejected. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-03 governs. Fault is then allocated from the chat log for compensation only. EV-CHAT-09105 shows the rider naming the correct sub-location twice — 'I am at Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign' at 13:05:05 and 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' at 13:06:35 — while the driver posted at 13:06:00 that he was at the mall taxi stand; the driver's own statement confirms he 'did not move to Tower B' before cancelling. That is POL-NS-03(i): the rider stated the tower and the driver did not move to it, so the driver bears the loss and receives nothing. POL-NS-03(ii), which the driver invokes, requires that neither party specified a sub-location; the rider plainly did, so that limb is unavailable and the goodwill does not arise. The rider's POL-NS-04 presence evidence is noted but does not need to carry the case, and in any event POL-NS-04's own limb (b) fails because the driver replied within 120 seconds.

Artifact weight and integrity (POL-GEN-02(3)): the findings rest on EV-GPS-09105, EV-TRIP-09105, EV-CHAT-09105 and EV-FARE-09105, each at weight 1.0, and none is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) — no clock skew (the 13:05:20 arrival marker sits on a fix), no trace gap (34 fixes, max gap 0.0 s), the chat log holds all 4 messages trip_record.chat_message_count records with an unbroken msg_id sequence, and the SGD 4.00 fee equals fee_schedule.resolution_rule for LARGE_VENUE and RYDE_X. The only discounted artifact, EV-ADVIS-09105-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, weight 0.0, MISSING, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact: its absence means POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable, and nothing in this ruling depends on it. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires — no unresolved contradiction, no repeat-party counter, no anti-farming pattern (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4 and the rate test), and the deciding facts are carried by unimpaired artifacts. No adverse finding rests on any context-only profile field. The disputed SGD 4.00 is refunded to the rider; the driver receives no compensation; no referral is produced.

ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace defeats the arrival limb. All 34 driver fixes in EV-GPS-09105 sit 219.77 m from the pickup pin (min, mean and max distance are identical, and trace_distance_km is 0.0), and the derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count of 0 — not one fix falls inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, and under POL-NS-02 that failure entitles the rider to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The in-geofence dwell is zero, so the waiting-period condition fails independently of the arrival limb. The driver's trace runs from 13:05:00 to cancellation at 13:10:30 with every fix at 0.0 km/h and zero distance travelled, but at 219.77 m from the pin, so the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup — a 300 second shortfall. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive: all four limbs must hold and any single failure makes the fee unchargeable. I accept that limb (a) is met (trip_record arrived_at 13:05:20) and that limb (d) is met (terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW), but limbs (b) and (c) both fail on the trace — no qualifying in-radius fix and no qualifying dwell. Two broken limbs, not one, defeat the charge.

This is the wrong-entrance case that POL-NS-03 governs. The driver was stationary — all fixes 0.0 km/h and trace_distance_km 0.0 — for 330 seconds, from 13:05:00 to the 13:10:30 cancellation, which is longer than the required 300 second dwell, at a point 219.77 m from the pickup pin: outside the 120 m POL-NS-02 arrival radius but comfortably inside the 400 m ceiling that is the whole test. On those numbers the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. POL-NS-05 is not engaged on these numbers (219.77 m is short of 300 m and the driver was not moving), and POL-NS-05 itself directs a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03.

Fault sits with the driver, so no compensation is payable to him. The chat log shows the rider naming the correct sub-location twice — 'I am at Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign' at 13:05:05 and 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' at 13:06:35 — while the driver had posted at 13:06:00 that he was at the mall taxi stand and never moved before cancelling at 13:10:30. That is the driver's own account on file: he waited at a mall entrance for the timer and did not move to Tower B. Under POL-NS-03(i), where the rider stated the correct entrance, block or tower in the chat log and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. The pin-ambiguity goodwill in limb (ii) is unavailable because it requires that neither party specified a sub-location, and the rider plainly did.

The driver cannot rebuild a dwell under POL-NS-06(i). The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09105-01, is MISSING — status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, weight_multiplier 0.0, payload null — so no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT advisory covers this pickup road and waiting window, and limb (i) is unavailable on its own terms. I rely on that artifact for its absence, which is itself citable. In any event there is nothing to accumulate: the trace records run_count 0 and accumulated dwell 0.0 seconds, i.e. no in-geofence interval existed at all.

The rider was at the pin rather than absent, which answers the driver's account that he was left waiting for a rider who never came. The rider track in EV-GPS-09105 carries 16 fixes, every one of them 25.0 m from the pickup pin (min and mean identical) and therefore inside the 150 m rider-presence measure that POL-NS-04 limb (c) sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 16 of 16. I put this forward as the presence test POL-NS-04 limb (c) defines rather than as a full limb (a)-to-(c) case, since the driver did reply at 13:06:00 within 120 seconds of the rider's first message; the rider's position also disposes of any suggestion that the rider's own absence explains the failed pickup.

The driver's compensation route is closed on this record. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here POL-NS-01 fails at limbs (b) and (c), and both POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 displace it. No compensation is payable to the driver, and the rider should not be charged over so that any payout can be funded.

The rider presently carries the disputed charge and needs the cancellation-fee line refunded. EV-FARE-09105 records cancellation_fee 4.00 SGD, total_charged 4.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, against a LARGE_VENUE pickup in an RYDE_X vehicle — the 4.00 SGD figure the fee schedule prescribes for both those dimensions, so no amount is in issue, only whether it may be kept. Because this dispute is filed by the rider, a NO_ACTION outcome would leave that 4.00 SGD charge standing under POL-GEN-03; the rider needs the cancellation-fee line refunded and nothing else on the fare is in dispute.

The trip_record 'arrived' marker is not a false arrival under POL-NS-05. At the 13:05:20 event the GPS trace places the driver stationary — 0.0 kph across all 34 fixes — at a mean 219.77 m from the pickup pin, which is inside POL-NS-05's 300 m ceiling and nothing like its 15 km/h motion trigger. POL-NS-05 therefore catches nothing: the driver is not to be written up as a false-arrival offender, the waiting period is not voided on that ground, and the case is decided under POL-NS-03.

The driver was at the venue and held his ground for the whole waiting window: 34 fixes at 0.0 kph, continuous from 13:05:00 to 13:10:30 — 330 seconds, more than the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum — all at 219.77 m from the pin. That is outside the 120 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for LARGE_VENUE but comfortably inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, which is precisely the wrong-entrance situation POL-NS-03 was written for. The fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 limb (b), and POL-NS-03 governs.

Both parties were on the same mall site, at different faces of it, and that is established from party statements in the chat log, not from geography: the driver posted at 13:06:00 'I am waiting at the mall taxi stand' and the rider answered at 13:06:35 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' This is the ordinary Singapore wrong-entrance case inside one LARGE_VENUE site carrying 3 registered pickup points, and the mislocation is between two signed points of that single venue.

On POL-NS-03(ii) the driver is owed the platform-funded pin-ambiguity goodwill of 50 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 2.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. The limb's second condition is satisfied outright: trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 3, above the threshold of 2. The first condition is satisfied as well, because neither party specified a sub-location: the rider's 13:05:05 message repeats the pickup pin's own label word for word ('Tower B ride-hail pickup'), and the driver's 13:06:00 message names only the mall taxi stand — neither party identified which of the three registered pickup points was to be used. The mislocation is therefore attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party.

POL-NS-04 does not apply and cannot strip the driver of compensation. The clause is conjunctive and limb (b) is not met: the rider's locating message at 13:05:05 drew the driver's reply at 13:06:00, 55 seconds later and well inside the 120 second window, and the exchange continued on both sides through the waiting window. The clause's target is an unanswered rider; that is not this trip, so the dispute stays under POL-NS-03 where the driver's goodwill payment is assessed.

Nothing in the bundle is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08, so the facts that decide this case carry full weight and none of the POL-NS-09 escalation triggers fires. The 13:05:20 'arrived' event sits within one 10 second sampling interval of the nearest fix (no clock skew, no gap, 34 fixes across the window); the chat log holds all 4 messages that trip_record.chat_message_count records, with no break in its msg_id sequence; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee exactly equals fee_schedule.resolution_rule for LARGE_VENUE (SGD 4.00) against RYDE_X (SGD 4.00). The driver's entitlement can be ruled on at full confidence.

The driver's pin-ambiguity goodwill is an independent payment under POL-GEN-03 and is not netted against anything else in the case: the SGD 2.00 is platform-funded and payable to the driver for the mislocation, and it stands on its own rather than being offset against the rider's side of the ledger.
